messages.content: What is HoneySQL and how do I get started with it?

HoneySQL is a library that lets you write SQL as Clojure data structures. Instead of string concatenation or templates, you build queries as maps and vectors.

**Setup**
```clojure
;; deps.edn
{:deps {com.github.seancorfield/honeysql {:mvn/version "2.5.1103"}}}

(require '[honey.sql :as sql]
         '[honey.sql.helpers :as h])
```

**Basic Query Structure**
```clojure
;; Queries are Clojure maps
{:select [:id :name :email]
 :from [:users]
 :where [:= :active true]}

;; Format to SQL string + parameters
(sql/format {:select [:id :name]
             :from [:users]
             :where [:= :id 1]})
;; => ["SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = ?" 1]
```

**Two Styles: Map vs Helpers**
```clojure
;; Style 1: Direct map (good for simple queries)
(sql/format
  {:select [:*]
   :from [:users]
   :where [:= :active true]
   :order-by [[:name :asc]]
   :limit 10})

;; Style 2: Helper functions (good for composition)
(-> (h/select :*)
    (h/from :users)
    (h/where [:= :active true])
    (h/order-by [:name :asc])
    (h/limit 10)
    sql/format)

;; Both produce the same SQL:
;; ["SELECT * FROM users WHERE active = ? ORDER BY name ASC LIMIT ?" true 10]
```

**Select**
```clojure
;; Select columns
{:select [:id :name :email]}
;; SELECT id, name, email

;; Select all
{:select [:*]}
;; SELECT *

;; Select with alias
{:select [[:id :user_id] [:name :user_name]]}
;; SELECT id AS user_id, name AS user_name

;; Select distinct
{:select-distinct [:category]}
;; SELECT DISTINCT category

;; Select with table prefix
{:select [:u.id :u.name :p.bio]
 :from [[:users :u]]
 :join [[:profiles :p] [:= :p.user_id :u.id]]}
;; SELECT u.id, u.name, p.bio FROM users AS u JOIN profiles AS p ON p.user_id = u.id
```

**From**
```clojure
;; Simple from
{:from [:users]}
;; FROM users

;; With alias
{:from [[:users :u]]}
;; FROM users AS u

;; Multiple tables
{:from [:users :orders]}
;; FROM users, orders

;; Subquery
{:select [:*]
 :from [[{:select [:*]
          :from [:users]
          :where [:= :active true]} :active_users]]}
;; SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM users WHERE active = ?) AS active_users
```

**Complete Example**
```clojure
(require '[next.jdbc :as jdbc])

(def ds (jdbc/get-datasource db-spec))

(defn find-active-users [role limit]
  (jdbc/execute! ds
    (sql/format
      {:select [:id :name :email :role]
       :from [:users]
       :where [:and
               [:= :active true]
               [:= :role role]]
       :order-by [[:created_at :desc]]
       :limit limit})))

(find-active-users "admin" 10)
;; Executes: SELECT id, name, email, role FROM users 
;;           WHERE (active = ? AND role = ?) 
;;           ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?
;; With params: [true "admin" 10]
```

**Format Options**
```clojure
;; Pretty print (for debugging)
(sql/format query {:pretty true})

;; Different parameter style
(sql/format query {:numbered true})  ; $1, $2 (PostgreSQL)
(sql/format query {:inline true})    ; Values inlined (DANGER!)

;; Dialect-specific
(sql/format query {:dialect :mysql})
(sql/format query {:dialect :sqlserver})
(sql/format query {:dialect :oracle})
```
How do I build complex WHERE clauses in HoneySQL?

HoneySQL uses vectors to represent SQL expressions. The first element is the operator, followed by operands.

**Basic Comparisons**
```clojure
;; Equality
[:= :id 1]              ; id = ?
[:!= :status "deleted"] ; status != ? (or <>)
[:<> :status "deleted"] ; status <> ?

;; Numeric comparisons
[:< :age 30]            ; age < ?
[:> :price 100]         ; price > ?
[:<= :quantity 50]      ; quantity <= ?
[:>= :score 80]         ; score >= ?

;; Example query
(sql/format
  {:select [:*]
   :from [:products]
   :where [:and
           [:>= :price 10]
           [:<= :price 100]]})
;; => ["SELECT * FROM products WHERE (price >= ? AND price <= ?)" 10 100]
```

**NULL Handling**
```clojure
;; IS NULL
[:= :deleted_at nil]    ; deleted_at IS NULL
[:is :deleted_at nil]   ; deleted_at IS NULL (explicit)

;; IS NOT NULL  
[:!= :email nil]        ; email IS NOT NULL
[:is-not :email nil]    ; email IS NOT NULL (explicit)

;; Note: HoneySQL converts nil comparisons automatically
{:where [:= :deleted_at nil]}
;; => "WHERE deleted_at IS NULL"
```

**Logical Operators**
```clojure
;; AND
[:and
  [:= :active true]
  [:= :verified true]
  [:> :age 18]]
;; (active = ? AND verified = ? AND age > ?)

;; OR
[:or
  [:= :role "admin"]
  [:= :role "moderator"]
  [:= :role "owner"]]
;; (role = ? OR role = ? OR role = ?)

;; NOT
[:not [:= :banned true]]
;; NOT (banned = ?)

;; Complex nesting
[:and
  [:= :active true]
  [:or
    [:= :role "admin"]
    [:and
      [:= :role "user"]
      [:= :verified true]]]]
;; (active = ? AND (role = ? OR (role = ? AND verified = ?)))
```

**IN and NOT IN**
```clojure
;; IN
[:in :status ["pending" "processing" "shipped"]]
;; status IN (?, ?, ?)

;; NOT IN
[:not-in :category ["archived" "deleted"]]
;; category NOT IN (?, ?)

;; Empty IN (returns nothing)
[:in :id []]            
;; id IN () -- always false

;; Subquery IN
[:in :user_id {:select [:id] :from [:admins]}]
;; user_id IN (SELECT id FROM admins)
```

**LIKE and Pattern Matching**
```clojure
;; LIKE
[:like :name "John%"]
;; name LIKE ?

;; ILIKE (case-insensitive, PostgreSQL)
[:ilike :email "%@gmail.com"]
;; email ILIKE ?

;; NOT LIKE
[:not-like :name "test%"]
;; name NOT LIKE ?

;; Dynamic pattern
(defn search-users [term]
  {:select [:*]
   :from [:users]
   :where [:ilike :name (str "%" term "%")]})
```

**BETWEEN**
```clojure
;; BETWEEN
[:between :age 18 65]
;; age BETWEEN ? AND ?

;; Date range
[:between :created_at #inst "2024-01-01" #inst "2024-12-31"]
;; created_at BETWEEN ? AND ?

;; NOT BETWEEN
[:not [:between :price 0 10]]
;; NOT (price BETWEEN ? AND ?)
```

**EXISTS**
```clojure
[:exists {:select [1]
          :from [:orders]
          :where [:= :orders.user_id :users.id]}]
;; EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders WHERE orders.user_id = users.id)

;; Find users with orders
{:select [:*]
 :from [:users]
 :where [:exists {:select [1]
                  :from [:orders]
                  :where [:= :orders.user_id :users.id]}]}
```

**Raw SQL Expressions**
```clojure
;; When HoneySQL doesn't support something
[:raw "users.data->>'name' = ?" "John"]
;; users.data->>'name' = ?

;; Or use :inline for raw (no parameterization)
{:where [:= :status [:inline "active"]]}
;; WHERE status = 'active'  (inlined, careful with SQL injection!)
```

**Conditional WHERE Building**
```clojure
(defn search-products [{:keys [name category min-price max-price in-stock?]}]
  (let [base {:select [:*]
              :from [:products]}]
    (cond-> base
      name       (h/where [:ilike :name (str "%" name "%")])
      category   (h/where [:= :category category])
      min-price  (h/where [:>= :price min-price])
      max-price  (h/where [:<= :price max-price])
      in-stock?  (h/where [:> :stock 0]))))

;; Usage
(sql/format (search-products {:name "laptop" :min-price 500}))
;; => ["SELECT * FROM products WHERE (name ILIKE ? AND price >= ?)" "%laptop%" 500]

(sql/format (search-products {:category "electronics" :in-stock? true}))
;; => ["SELECT * FROM products WHERE (category = ? AND stock > ?)" "electronics" 0]
```

**Composing WHERE Clauses**
```clojure
;; Helper functions that return where clauses
(defn active-filter [] [:= :active true])
(defn role-filter [role] [:= :role role])
(defn verified-filter [] [:= :verified true])

;; Combine them
(defn admin-query []
  {:select [:*]
   :from [:users]
   :where [:and
           (active-filter)
           (role-filter "admin")
           (verified-filter)]})

;; Or dynamically
(defn build-query [filters]
  {:select [:*]
   :from [:users]
   :where (into [:and] filters)})

(build-query [(active-filter) (role-filter "user")])
```
How do I use JOINs in HoneySQL?

HoneySQL supports all standard SQL join types with a clean syntax.

**Basic JOIN Syntax**
```clojure
;; Structure: [table-spec join-condition]
{:select [:*]
 :from [:users]
 :join [:orders [:= :orders.user_id :users.id]]}
;; SELECT * FROM users JOIN orders ON orders.user_id = users.id

;; With table alias
{:select [:u.* :o.total]
 :from [[:users :u]]
 :join [[:orders :o] [:= :o.user_id :u.id]]}
;; SELECT u.*, o.total FROM users AS u JOIN orders AS o ON o.user_id = u.id
```

**Join Types**
```clojure
;; INNER JOIN (default)
{:from [:users]
 :join [:orders [:= :orders.user_id :users.id]]}
;; JOIN orders ON ...

;; LEFT JOIN
{:from [:users]
 :left-join [:orders [:= :orders.user_id :users.id]]}
;; LEFT JOIN orders ON ...

;; RIGHT JOIN
{:from [:users]
 :right-join [:orders [:= :orders.user_id :users.id]]}
;; RIGHT JOIN orders ON ...

;; FULL OUTER JOIN
{:from [:users]
 :full-join [:orders [:= :orders.user_id :users.id]]}
;; FULL JOIN orders ON ...

;; CROSS JOIN
{:from [:users]
 :cross-join [:products]}
;; CROSS JOIN products
```

**Multiple Joins**
```clojure
;; Multiple tables in one join clause
{:select [:o.id :u.name :p.title :c.name]
 :from [[:orders :o]]
 :join [[:users :u] [:= :u.id :o.user_id]
        [:products :p] [:= :p.id :o.product_id]
        [:categories :c] [:= :c.id :p.category_id]]
 :where [:= :o.status "completed"]}

;; Produces:
;; SELECT o.id, u.name, p.title, c.name
;; FROM orders AS o
;; JOIN users AS u ON u.id = o.user_id
;; JOIN products AS p ON p.id = o.product_id
;; JOIN categories AS c ON c.id = p.category_id
;; WHERE o.status = ?

;; Mixed join types
{:select [:u.name :o.total :p.bio]
 :from [[:users :u]]
 :join [[:orders :o] [:= :o.user_id :u.id]]
 :left-join [[:profiles :p] [:= :p.user_id :u.id]]}
;; JOIN orders ... LEFT JOIN profiles ...
```

**Complex Join Conditions**
```clojure
;; Multiple conditions with AND
{:select [:*]
 :from [:users]
 :join [:subscriptions [:and
                         [:= :subscriptions.user_id :users.id]
                         [:= :subscriptions.active true]]]}
;; JOIN subscriptions ON (subscriptions.user_id = users.id AND subscriptions.active = ?)

;; With OR
{:from [:users]
 :join [:roles [:or
                 [:= :roles.user_id :users.id]
                 [:= :roles.inherited_from :users.role_id]]]}

;; Value comparisons in join
{:from [:orders]
 :join [:discounts [:and
                     [:= :discounts.product_id :orders.product_id]
                     [:>= :orders.quantity :discounts.min_quantity]]]}
```

**Self Joins**
```clojure
;; Employees with managers (same table)
{:select [:e.name [:m.name :manager_name]]
 :from [[:employees :e]]
 :left-join [[:employees :m] [:= :m.id :e.manager_id]]}
;; SELECT e.name, m.name AS manager_name
;; FROM employees AS e
;; LEFT JOIN employees AS m ON m.id = e.manager_id

;; Find duplicate emails
{:select [:u1.id :u1.email]
 :from [[:users :u1]]
 :join [[:users :u2] [:and
                       [:= :u1.email :u2.email]
                       [:<> :u1.id :u2.id]]]}
```

**Using Helpers**
```clojure
(-> (h/select :u.* :p.bio :p.avatar)
    (h/from [:users :u])
    (h/left-join [:profiles :p] [:= :p.user_id :u.id])
    (h/join [:roles :r] [:= :r.id :u.role_id])
    (h/where [:= :u.active true])
    sql/format)

;; Building joins dynamically
(defn with-profile [query]
  (h/left-join query [:profiles :p] [:= :p.user_id :u.id]))

(defn with-orders [query]
  (h/left-join query [:orders :o] [:= :o.user_id :u.id]))

(-> (h/select :u.*)
    (h/from [:users :u])
    with-profile
    with-orders
    sql/format)
```

**Subquery Joins**
```clojure
;; Join with subquery
{:select [:u.name :order_stats.total_orders :order_stats.total_spent]
 :from [[:users :u]]
 :left-join [[{:select [:user_id
                        [:%count.* :total_orders]
                        [:%sum.total :total_spent]]
               :from [:orders]
               :group-by [:user_id]} :order_stats]
             [:= :order_stats.user_id :u.id]]}
;; SELECT u.name, order_stats.total_orders, order_stats.total_spent
;; FROM users AS u
;; LEFT JOIN (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS total_orders, SUM(total) AS total_spent
;;            FROM orders GROUP BY user_id) AS order_stats
;; ON order_stats.user_id = u.id
```

**Complete Example**
```clojure
(defn order-details-query [order-id]
  {:select [:o.id
            :o.created_at
            :o.status
            [:u.name :customer_name]
            [:u.email :customer_email]
            [:p.title :product_title]
            [:p.price :unit_price]
            :oi.quantity
            [[:* :p.price :oi.quantity] :line_total]]
   :from [[:orders :o]]
   :join [[:users :u] [:= :u.id :o.user_id]
          [:order_items :oi] [:= :oi.order_id :o.id]
          [:products :p] [:= :p.id :oi.product_id]]
   :where [:= :o.id order-id]
   :order-by [[:oi.id :asc]]})

(jdbc/execute! ds (sql/format (order-details-query 123)))
```
How do I handle aggregations and GROUP BY in HoneySQL?

HoneySQL provides special function syntax for aggregations using the `:%function.column` pattern.

**Aggregate Functions Syntax**
```clojure
;; Syntax: :%function.column or [:%function :column]
:%count.*              ; COUNT(*)
:%count.id             ; COUNT(id)
[:%count :id]          ; COUNT(id) - alternative syntax
:%sum.amount           ; SUM(amount)
:%avg.price            ; AVG(price)
:%min.created_at       ; MIN(created_at)
:%max.score            ; MAX(score)
:%count-distinct.user_id ; COUNT(DISTINCT user_id)
```

**Basic Aggregation**
```clojure
(sql/format
  {:select [[:%count.* :total]]
   :from [:users]})
;; => ["SELECT COUNT(*) AS total FROM users"]

(sql/format
  {:select [[:%count.* :total]
            [:%sum.balance :total_balance]
            [:%avg.age :average_age]]
   :from [:users]
   :where [:= :active true]})
;; => ["SELECT COUNT(*) AS total, SUM(balance) AS total_balance, AVG(age) AS average_age FROM users WHERE active = ?" true]
```

**GROUP BY**
```clojure
;; Simple group by
{:select [:role [:%count.* :count]]
 :from [:users]
 :group-by [:role]}
;; SELECT role, COUNT(*) AS count FROM users GROUP BY role

;; Multiple group columns
{:select [:year :month [:%sum.revenue :total_revenue]]
 :from [:sales]
 :group-by [:year :month]
 :order-by [[:year :desc] [:month :desc]]}

;; Group by with expression
{:select [[[:date_trunc "month" :created_at] :month]
          [:%count.* :signups]]
 :from [:users]
 :group-by [[:date_trunc "month" :created_at]]}
```

**HAVING**
```clojure
;; Filter aggregated results
{:select [:category [:%count.* :product_count]]
 :from [:products]
 :group-by [:category]
 :having [:> :%count.* 10]}
;; SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS product_count
;; FROM products GROUP BY category HAVING COUNT(*) > ?

;; Complex HAVING
{:select [:user_id
          [:%count.* :order_count]
          [:%sum.total :total_spent]]
 :from [:orders]
 :where [:>= :created_at #inst "2024-01-01"]
 :group-by [:user_id]
 :having [:and
          [:>= :%count.* 5]
          [:>= :%sum.total 1000]]
 :order-by [[:%sum.total :desc]]}
```

**Common Aggregation Patterns**
```clojure
;; Count by category
(defn count-by-category [ds]
  (jdbc/execute! ds
    (sql/format
      {:select [:category [:%count.* :count]]
       :from [:products]
       :group-by [:category]
       :order-by [[:%count.* :desc]]})))

;; Daily stats
(defn daily-stats [ds start-date end-date]
  (jdbc/execute! ds
    (sql/format
      {:select [[[:date :created_at] :day]
                [:%count.* :total_orders]
                [:%sum.total :revenue]
                [:%avg.total :avg_order_value]]
       :from [:orders]
       :where [:between :created_at start-date end-date]
       :group-by [[:date :created_at]]
       :order-by [[:day :asc]]})))

;; Top N query
(defn top-customers [ds n]
  (jdbc/execute! ds
    (sql/format
      {:select [:u.id :u.name [:%count.o.id :order_count] [:%sum.o.total :total_spent]]
       :from [[:users :u]]
       :join [[:orders :o] [:= :o.user_id :u.id]]
       :group-by [:u.id :u.name]
       :order-by [[:%sum.o.total :desc]]
       :limit n})))
```

**Window Functions**
```clojure
;; ROW_NUMBER
{:select [:id :name :salary
          [[[:over [:row_number]
             {:partition-by :department
              :order-by [[:salary :desc]]}] :rank]]]
 :from [:employees]}
;; SELECT id, name, salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rank
;; FROM employees

;; Running total
{:select [:date :amount
          [[[:over [:sum :amount]
             {:order-by [:date]
              :frame [:rows :unbounded-preceding :current-row]}] :running_total]]]
 :from [:transactions]}

;; Multiple window functions
{:select [:id :department :salary
          [[[:over [:rank] {:partition-by :department :order-by [[:salary :desc]]}] :dept_rank]]
          [[[:over [:rank] {:order-by [[:salary :desc]]}] :company_rank]]
          [[[:over [:avg :salary] {:partition-by :department}] :dept_avg]]]
 :from [:employees]}
```

**Distinct Counts**
```clojure
;; COUNT(DISTINCT ...)
{:select [[:%count-distinct.user_id :unique_users]
          [:%count.* :total_sessions]]
 :from [:sessions]
 :where [:>= :created_at #inst "2024-01-01"]}
;; SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS unique_users, COUNT(*) AS total_sessions ...

;; Distinct with group by
{:select [:date
          [:%count-distinct.user_id :daily_active_users]
          [:%count.* :total_events]]
 :from [:events]
 :group-by [:date]}
```

**Aggregate with CASE**
```clojure
;; Conditional aggregation
{:select [[:%sum [:case [:= :status "completed"] :amount :else 0]] :completed_revenue]
         [:%sum [:case [:= :status "pending"] :amount :else 0]] :pending_revenue]
         [:%count [:case [:= :status "cancelled"] 1]] :cancelled_count]]
 :from [:orders]}

;; Pivot-style query
{:select [:product_id
          [:%sum [:case [:= :month 1] :sales :else 0]] :jan]
          [:%sum [:case [:= :month 2] :sales :else 0]] :feb]
          [:%sum [:case [:= :month 3] :sales :else 0]] :mar]]
 :from [:monthly_sales]
 :where [:= :year 2024]
 :group-by [:product_id]}
```

**Building Dynamic Reports**
```clojure
(defn sales-report [{:keys [group-by-field date-range]}]
  (let [group-col (keyword group-by-field)]
    {:select [group-col
              [:%count.* :order_count]
              [:%sum.total :revenue]
              [:%avg.total :avg_order]]
     :from [:orders]
     :where [:between :created_at (:start date-range) (:end date-range)]
     :group-by [group-col]
     :order-by [[:%sum.total :desc]]}))

;; By category
(sales-report {:group-by-field "category"
               :date-range {:start #inst "2024-01-01" :end #inst "2024-12-31"}})

;; By region
(sales-report {:group-by-field "region"
               :date-range {:start #inst "2024-01-01" :end #inst "2024-12-31"}})
```
How do I use CTEs (Common Table Expressions) and subqueries in HoneySQL?

HoneySQL supports both CTEs (WITH clauses) and subqueries for complex queries.

**Common Table Expressions (CTEs)**
```clojure
;; Basic CTE with :with
{:with [[:active_users {:select [:*]
                         :from [:users]
                         :where [:= :active true]}]]
 :select [:*]
 :from [:active_users]
 :where [:> :login_count 10]}
;; WITH active_users AS (SELECT * FROM users WHERE active = ?)
;; SELECT * FROM active_users WHERE login_count > ?

;; Multiple CTEs
{:with [[:recent_orders {:select [:*]
                          :from [:orders]
                          :where [:> :created_at #inst "2024-01-01"]}]
        [:high_value {:select [:*]
                      :from [:recent_orders]
                      :where [:> :total 1000]}]]
 :select [:user_id [:%count.* :order_count] [:%sum.total :total_spent]]
 :from [:high_value]
 :group-by [:user_id]}
```

**Recursive CTEs**
```clojure
;; Hierarchical data (org chart)
{:with-recursive [[:employee_hierarchy
                   {:union-all
                    [{:select [:id :name :manager_id [[:cast 1 :int] :level]]
                      :from [:employees]
                      :where [:is :manager_id nil]}  ; Root nodes
                     {:select [:e.id :e.name :e.manager_id [[:+ :eh.level 1] :level]]
                      :from [[:employees :e]]
                      :join [[:employee_hierarchy :eh] [:= :eh.id :e.manager_id]]}]}]]
 :select [:*]
 :from [:employee_hierarchy]
 :order-by [:level :name]}

;; Generates:
;; WITH RECURSIVE employee_hierarchy AS (
;;   SELECT id, name, manager_id, CAST(1 AS int) AS level
;;   FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL
;;   UNION ALL
;;   SELECT e.id, e.name, e.manager_id, eh.level + 1 AS level
;;   FROM employees AS e
;;   JOIN employee_hierarchy AS eh ON eh.id = e.manager_id
;; )
;; SELECT * FROM employee_hierarchy ORDER BY level, name
```

**Subqueries in SELECT**
```clojure
;; Scalar subquery
{:select [:u.*
          [{:select [[:%count.*]]
            :from [:orders]
            :where [:= :orders.user_id :u.id]} :order_count]]
 :from [[:users :u]]}
;; SELECT u.*, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE orders.user_id = u.id) AS order_count
;; FROM users AS u

;; Multiple scalar subqueries
{:select [:p.id :p.name
          [{:select [[:%avg.rating]]
            :from [:reviews]
            :where [:= :reviews.product_id :p.id]} :avg_rating]
          [{:select [[:%count.*]]
            :from [:order_items]
            :where [:= :order_items.product_id :p.id]} :times_ordered]]
 :from [[:products :p]]}
```

**Subqueries in FROM**
```clojure
;; Derived table
{:select [:top_users.*]
 :from [[{:select [:user_id [:%sum.total :total_spent]]
          :from [:orders]
          :group-by [:user_id]
          :having [:> :%sum.total 10000]} :top_users]]}

;; Join with subquery
{:select [:u.name :user_stats.order_count :user_stats.total_spent]
 :from [[:users :u]]
 :join [[{:select [:user_id
                   [:%count.* :order_count]
                   [:%sum.total :total_spent]]
          :from [:orders]
          :group-by [:user_id]} :user_stats]
        [:= :user_stats.user_id :u.id]]
 :order-by [[:user_stats.total_spent :desc]]}
```

**Subqueries in WHERE**
```clojure
;; IN with subquery
{:select [:*]
 :from [:products]
 :where [:in :category_id
         {:select [:id]
          :from [:categories]
          :where [:= :featured true]}]}
;; SELECT * FROM products WHERE category_id IN (SELECT id FROM categories WHERE featured = ?)

;; EXISTS
{:select [:*]
 :from [:users]
 :where [:exists {:select [1]
                  :from [:orders]
                  :where [:and
                          [:= :orders.user_id :users.id]
                          [:> :orders.total 100]]}]}
;; SELECT * FROM users WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders WHERE orders.user_id = users.id AND orders.total > ?)

;; NOT EXISTS
{:select [:*]
 :from [:products]
 :where [:not-exists {:select [1]
                      :from [:order_items]
                      :where [:= :order_items.product_id :products.id]}]}
;; Products never ordered

;; Comparison with subquery
{:select [:*]
 :from [:employees]
 :where [:> :salary {:select [[:%avg.salary]]
                     :from [:employees]}]}
;; Employees earning above average
```

**Complex CTE Example**
```clojure
(defn monthly-retention-report [ds year month]
  (jdbc/execute! ds
    (sql/format
      {:with [;; Users active in target month
              [:target_month_users
               {:select-distinct [:user_id]
                :from [:events]
                :where [:and
                        [:= [:extract :year :created_at] year]
                        [:= [:extract :month :created_at] month]]}]
              ;; Users active in previous month
              [:prev_month_users
               {:select-distinct [:user_id]
                :from [:events]
                :where [:and
                        [:= [:extract :year :created_at] (if (= month 1) (dec year) year)]
                        [:= [:extract :month :created_at] (if (= month 1) 12 (dec month))]]}]
              ;; Retained users (in both months)
              [:retained_users
               {:select [:t.user_id]
                :from [[:target_month_users :t]]
                :join [[:prev_month_users :p] [:= :t.user_id :p.user_id]]}]]
       :select [[:inline year] :year]
               [[:inline month] :month]
               [{:select [[:%count.*]] :from [:prev_month_users]} :prev_month_count]
               [{:select [[:%count.*]] :from [:target_month_users]} :current_month_count]
               [{:select [[:%count.*]] :from [:retained_users]} :retained_count]]})))
```

**Building CTEs Dynamically**
```clojure
(defn with-cte [query cte-name cte-query]
  (update query :with (fnil conj []) [cte-name cte-query]))

(defn build-analysis-query [filters]
  (-> {:select [:*] :from [:analysis_view]}
      (with-cte :filtered_data
        {:select [:*]
         :from [:raw_data]
         :where (build-where filters)})
      (with-cte :analysis_view
        {:select [:category [:%count.* :count] [:%avg.value :avg_value]]
         :from [:filtered_data]
         :group-by [:category]})))
```
How do I use INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and UPSERT in HoneySQL?

HoneySQL provides clean syntax for all data modification statements.

**INSERT**
```clojure
;; Single row with column-value map
(sql/format
  {:insert-into :users
   :values [{:name "Alice" :email "alice@example.com" :active true}]})
;; => ["INSERT INTO users (name, email, active) VALUES (?, ?, ?)" "Alice" "alice@example.com" true]

;; Multiple rows
(sql/format
  {:insert-into :users
   :values [{:name "Alice" :email "alice@example.com"}
            {:name "Bob" :email "bob@example.com"}
            {:name "Charlie" :email "charlie@example.com"}]})
;; INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES (?, ?), (?, ?), (?, ?)

;; Explicit columns
(sql/format
  {:insert-into [:users [:name :email]]
   :values [["Alice" "alice@example.com"]
            ["Bob" "bob@example.com"]]})
;; INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES (?, ?), (?, ?)

;; RETURNING (PostgreSQL)
(sql/format
  {:insert-into :users
   :values [{:name "Alice"}]
   :returning [:id :created_at]})
;; INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?) RETURNING id, created_at

;; INSERT ... SELECT
(sql/format
  {:insert-into [:archived_users [:id :name :email]]
   :select [:id :name :email]
   :from [:users]
   :where [:< :last_login #inst "2023-01-01"]})
;; INSERT INTO archived_users (id, name, email) SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE last_login < ?
```

**Using Helpers**
```clojure
(require '[honey.sql.helpers :as h])

(-> (h/insert-into :users)
    (h/values [{:name "Alice" :email "alice@example.com"}])
    (h/returning :id)
    sql/format)

;; Columns helper
(-> (h/insert-into :users)
    (h/columns :name :email :role)
    (h/values [["Alice" "alice@example.com" "user"]
               ["Bob" "bob@example.com" "admin"]])
    sql/format)
```

**UPDATE**
```clojure
;; Basic update
(sql/format
  {:update :users
   :set {:name "Alicia" :updated_at [:now]}
   :where [:= :id 1]})
;; => ["UPDATE users SET name = ?, updated_at = NOW() WHERE id = ?" "Alicia" 1]

;; Increment/decrement
(sql/format
  {:update :products
   :set {:stock [:- :stock 1]
         :times_sold [:+ :times_sold 1]}
   :where [:= :id 123]})
;; UPDATE products SET stock = stock - ?, times_sold = times_sold + ? WHERE id = ?

;; With FROM (PostgreSQL)
(sql/format
  {:update :orders
   :set {:status "shipped"}
   :from [:shipments]
   :where [:and
           [:= :shipments.order_id :orders.id]
           [:= :shipments.status "delivered"]]})

;; RETURNING
(sql/format
  {:update :users
   :set {:password_hash "new_hash"}
   :where [:= :id 1]
   :returning [:id :email :updated_at]})

;; Conditional update with CASE
(sql/format
  {:update :products
   :set {:price [:case
                  [:< :stock 10] [:* :price 1.1]  ; Low stock: +10%
                  [:> :stock 100] [:* :price 0.9]  ; High stock: -10%
                  :else :price]}
   :where [:= :category "electronics"]})
```

**DELETE**
```clojure
;; Basic delete
(sql/format
  {:delete-from :users
   :where [:= :id 1]})
;; => ["DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ?" 1]

;; Delete with subquery
(sql/format
  {:delete-from :sessions
   :where [:in :user_id
           {:select [:id]
            :from [:users]
            :where [:= :banned true]}]})

;; Delete all (careful!)
(sql/format
  {:delete-from :temp_logs})
;; DELETE FROM temp_logs

;; RETURNING
(sql/format
  {:delete-from :notifications
   :where [:< :created_at #inst "2024-01-01"]
   :returning [:id :user_id]})

;; Truncate (faster for all rows)
(sql/format
  {:truncate :logs})
;; TRUNCATE logs
```

**UPSERT (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT)**
```clojure
;; PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE
(sql/format
  {:insert-into :users
   :values [{:email "alice@example.com" :name "Alice" :login_count 1}]
   :on-conflict [:email]
   :do-update-set [:name :login_count]})
;; INSERT INTO users (email, name, login_count) VALUES (?, ?, ?)
;; ON CONFLICT (email) DO UPDATE SET name = EXCLUDED.name, login_count = EXCLUDED.login_count

;; Increment on conflict
(sql/format
  {:insert-into :page_views
   :values [{:page_id 123 :view_count 1}]
   :on-conflict [:page_id]
   :do-update-set {:view_count [:+ :page_views.view_count 1]}})
;; ON CONFLICT (page_id) DO UPDATE SET view_count = page_views.view_count + 1

;; ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
(sql/format
  {:insert-into :users
   :values [{:email "alice@example.com" :name "Alice"}]
   :on-conflict [:email]
   :do-nothing true})
;; INSERT INTO users (email, name) VALUES (?, ?) ON CONFLICT (email) DO NOTHING

;; MySQL INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE
(sql/format
  {:insert-into :users
   :values [{:email "alice@example.com" :name "Alice"}]
   :on-duplicate-key-update {:name :values.name}}
  {:dialect :mysql})
```

**Batch Operations**
```clojure
(defn batch-insert! [ds table records]
  (when (seq records)
    (jdbc/execute! ds
      (sql/format
        {:insert-into table
         :values records}))))

(defn batch-upsert! [ds table records conflict-keys update-keys]
  (when (seq records)
    (jdbc/execute! ds
      (sql/format
        {:insert-into table
         :values records
         :on-conflict conflict-keys
         :do-update-set update-keys}))))

;; Usage
(batch-upsert! ds :products
  [{:sku "ABC" :name "Product A" :price 10}
   {:sku "DEF" :name "Product B" :price 20}]
  [:sku]
  [:name :price])
```

**Transaction Example**
```clojure
(defn transfer-funds! [ds from-id to-id amount]
  (jdbc/with-transaction [tx ds]
    ;; Deduct from source
    (jdbc/execute! tx
      (sql/format
        {:update :accounts
         :set {:balance [:- :balance amount]}
         :where [:and
                 [:= :id from-id]
                 [:>= :balance amount]]}))
    
    ;; Add to destination
    (jdbc/execute! tx
      (sql/format
        {:update :accounts
         :set {:balance [:+ :balance amount]}
         :where [:= :id to-id]}))
    
    ;; Log transaction
    (jdbc/execute! tx
      (sql/format
        {:insert-into :transactions
         :values [{:from_account from-id
                   :to_account to-id
                   :amount amount
                   :created_at [:now]}]}))))
```
